checks.item: Minimum wage 2026 - hourly rate (minimumWage.note)
checks.researched: 10,320 won an hour, applied from 1 Jan 2026 (+2.9%); 2027 already fixed at 10,700
checks.verified: 10,320 won an hour for 2026, +290 won / +2.9% on 10,030 (2025). The Minimum Wage Commission table lists 2024 = 9,860, 2025 = 10,030, 2026 = 10,320, 2027 = 10,700. One national rate, no sector or regional split.
checks.source: https://www.moel.go.kr/news/enews/report/enewsView.do?news_seq=18144 (Ministry of Employment and Labor: 2026 rate raised 290 won, 2.9%, to 10,320 an hour); https://www.minimumwage.go.kr/minWage/policy/decisionMain.do (Minimum Wage Commission table 2024-2027); https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/최저임금 (same table)
checks.note: Legal figure, exactly right. Checked against primary sources, not the colleague's KDI summary. The note string 'The minimum wage (₩10,320 an hour)' is 34 characters, well inside the ~70 limit. Confidence: high.

checks.item: Minimum wage 2026 - annual full-time figure and its arithmetic, 209-hour month including weekly-holiday pay (minimumWage.annualFullTime)
checks.researched: 25,882,560 won a year = 10,320 x 209 hours x 12 (2,156,880 a month); nothing added for a 13th month
checks.verified: Official monthly equivalent 2,156,880 won 'on a 40-hours-a-week, 209-hours-a-month basis'; x 12 = 25,882,560. 209 = 174 ordinary hours + 35 paid weekly-holiday hours, i.e. (40 + 8) x 365 / 7 / 12 = 208.6, rounded to 209. Check of the colleague's 2027 line: 10,700 x 209 = 2,236,300 a month, x 12 = 26,835,600 (matches the Commission table).
checks.source: https://www.moel.go.kr/news/enews/report/enewsView.do?news_seq=18144 (2,156,880 won a month, 주 40시간 월 209시간 기준); https://www.minimumwage.go.kr/minWage/policy/decisionMain.do (table header 월급 209시간 기준; 2026 = 2,156,880, 2027 = 2,236,300); https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/최저임금 (formula: minimum wage x 209 = 174 working hours + 35 paid weekly-holiday hours)
checks.note: Yes, this is the standard, official way: the Ministry and the Commission both publish the monthly floor as hourly x 209, and the 209 includes the paid weekly rest day (주휴) that Korean law gives staff working 15+ hours a week. Plain 2,080-hour arithmetic (10,320 x 2,080 = 21,465,600) would understate the legal monthly floor by about 17%. Korea has no statutory 13th or 14th month; severance accrual and employer social insurance are not part of the minimum wage. Confidence: high.

checks.item: Driving licence age, car licence without supervising driver (drivingAge)
checks.researched: 18 (Class 1 and Class 2 ordinary); motorised bicycle 16; Class 1 large/special 19 plus a year of experience
checks.verified: 18. Ministry of Government Legislation guide: 제1종 보통, 제2종 보통, 제2종 소형 = 18세 이상; 제1종 대형 and 특수 = 19세 이상 and at least 1 year after obtaining a Class 1 or 2 ordinary licence; 원동기장치자전거 = 16세 이상. No exception for under-18s driving a car.

checks.item: Bachelor tuition at a PUBLIC university, national vs private (tuition.bachelor.state)

checks.verified: 2026 averages (Ministry of Education / KCUE disclosure): national and public universities 4,250,000 (+0.3%); private universities 8,231,500 (+2.8%); all 192 four-year universities 7,273,000 (+2.1%); capital region 8,270,000, non-capital 6,619,600. checks.note: The researched number reproduces its source exactly (it is the all-university average), so this is a definitional gap, not an arithmetic error: it is 71% above the national/public figure (4,250,000) and 12% below private (8,231,500). Read literally ('state = mainstream public universities') the cell would be 4,250,000, but then the junior-college cell (6.65M) would cost more than state and break a community < state < elite ordering; the colleague chose the all-university average on purpose and recorded 4.25M in the source text. Caller's call. The claim that most students attend private universities was not re-checked. Confidence on the figures: high.

checks.verified: Ministry of Health and Welfare 2nd Health and Medical Workforce Survey, 2023 pay: nurses about 52M (51.95M), owners and employees combined, residents excluded. 1st survey, 2020 pay: nurses 47,448,594. checks.researched: 60,000,000 won (OECD statutory salary after 15 years converted and uplifted; pay table build-up 53-56M)
checks.verified: About 55-61M, central about 57M. checks.item: National median full-time annual gross wage (wageLevels.medianFullTime)
checks.researched: 42,500,000 won (derived from OECD ratios)
checks.verified: OECD 2025: the minimum wage is 59.57% of the median full-time wage (47.21% of the mean). Route 1: 2025 minimum 10,030 x 209 x 12 = 25,155,240 / 0.5957 = 42.2M. checks.item: CSAT (대학수학능력시험, suneung) scoring: scale, direction, grade shares, absolute subjects, standard scores, pass mark (schooling.gradeSystem)
checks.researched: Grade 1 (best) to 9 (worst) per subject, lower is better; Korean/maths/inquiry relative with shares 4/7/12/17/20/17/12/7/4%; English (90+ = grade 1) and Korean History absolute; standard scores mean 100 SD 20 (Korean, maths) and mean 50 SD 10 (inquiry); no national pass mark
checks.verified: Confirmed. Nine grades, 1 = best. Relative subjects: grade 1 = top 4%, then 7, 12, 17, 20, 17, 12, 7, 4% (cumulative 4, 11, 23, 40, 60, 77, 89, 96, 100). Absolute: English 90+ raw points = grade 1 then one grade per 10 points; Korean History 40+ = grade 1 then 5-point steps. Standard score S = z x SD + mean: Korean and mathematics mean 100, SD 20; other areas mean 50, SD 10. Grade 5 = 40th-60th percentile band.
checks.note: Two independent pages agree on the grade table and on absolute English and Korean History. No source states a pass mark (they report grades and standard scores only), consistent with the colleague's 'no national pass mark'. The 0-200 standard-score range was not re-checked. Confidence: high.

checks.item: Naeshin 5-level reform: levels and percentage shares (schooling.gradeSystem)
checks.researched: From the cohort entering high school in 2025 (2028 admissions) the school record becomes 5 levels (1-5, about 10/24/32/24/10%) and the CSAT becomes an integrated exam but keeps 9 grades
checks.verified: Confirmed in part: the Ministry plan converts the 9-level school record to a 5-level system, first for students who were in middle-school year 2 in 2023 (i.e. entering high school in 2025, 2028 admissions); the CSAT moves to an integrated format with no choice subjects and no change to its grade reporting is announced. The percentage shares of the five levels are NOT stated on the page and I could not reach another source (namu.wiki returned 403; the Wikipedia pages carry no shares).
checks.note: Only the 10/24/32/24/10 shares are unverified; they match my recollection of the Ministry's 2023 plan, but that is memory, not a fetched source. Design note: for any player who reaches high school from 2025 on, the school record is 1-5, so the 9-point CSAT grade is the only grade scale stable across all cohorts.
